chunks: Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding a woman who began the day fasting, then when the day had risen or it was evening, she menstruated: should she break her fast? He said, "Yes; and if it is before sunset, then she should break her fast."

And about a woman who sees purity at the beginning of the day in the Month of Ramadan, but she has not performed ghusl (ritual bath) and has not eaten anything, what should she do regarding that day? He said, "Her breaking of the fast is only due to the blood."

key_terms.الدَّمِ: the menstrual blood that is the cause of the ruling
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: sunset, the end of the fasting day
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan in which fasting is observed
key_terms.صَائِمَةً: fasting as a woman observing sawm

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman menstruates during a fast or becomes pure from menstruation during the day in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on fasting for a menstruating woman in Ramadan. If menstruation begins during the day, her fast is broken; if she becomes pure early in the day, the cause of not fasting was the blood itself.
